transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-04-07 10:00 PDT | Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Stratosense Head of ML), Ethan Cole (CTO), Liam O'Neill (Data Engineer), Sasha Kim (Product)

Summary:
- Goal: scope a 2-week POC to validate open-model selection for Stratosense's customer support summarization + multilingual routing workload.
- Success criteria: latency < 350ms p50 for single-turn summaries, F1/ROUGE thresholds comparable to current prod (internal baseline), cost <= target $X per 1M tokens (TBD), pass basic privacy/compliance checks for EU data.
- Next: Redwood to propose 3 open-model shortlist, draft benchmark plan; customer to provide prompt set and confirm compliance constraints.

Topics:
- Current stack + volume sizing
- Model quality tradeoffs and multilingual needs
- Benchmarks and runner approach
- Timeline and success metrics
- Security/compliance constraints

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our systems engineer. quick round robin?
[00:07] Marta: hi Marta here, head of ML, we own the summarization pipeline.
[00:11] Ethan: Ethan, CTO.
[00:14] Liam: Liam, infra and data.
[00:16] Sasha: Sasha, product.
[00:18] Priya: good to meet you all. quick agenda — we want to nail success criteria, sizing and pick models to test, yes?
[00:24] Marta: yes, that's right. we have two main flows: 1) customer support chat summarization and 2) multilingual routing — detect language and route to localized teams. current prod uses a smaller proprietary model with fine-tuning but it's noisy on long chats.
[00:40] Jordan: ok good. quick sizing — can you share daily volume?
[00:43] Liam: sure, average 40k messages/day, about 8k summarization calls/day, peak 18k. average context length ~ 1.2k tokens, summarization target output 100-250 tokens. multilingual traffic about 25% across 12 languages, mainly Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese.
[01:05] Priya: got it. for the POC we'd recommend a ~2-week run with 1k representative sessions/day for bench marking; that gives stable metrics while keeping cost low. does that align?
[01:14] Marta: yes that sounds fine. success criteria — we want p50 latency < 350ms for single-turn summary generation in hosted mode; quality at or above our current ROUGE-1 ~0.58 baseline — also human eval for top-100.
[01:28] Jordan: noted. also please confirm any hard compliance rules — EU data residency, SOC2, KMS, etc.
[01:34] Ethan: EU data residency required for EU customers, we have SAML SSO and we need logs for audits. KMS integration preferred but not blocking for POC if data anonymized.
[01:44] Priya: for bench we'll simulate EU residency by routing to EU region and apply masking. on models — we propose testing 3 open-models: 1) Mistral-7B-v2-like opti (high quality on instruction tasks, good latency), 2) Falcon-40B-instruct-ish (strong on long-context but heavier), 3) Llama 2 13B quantized baseline (cheap, decent multilingual). any immediate red flags?
[02:10] Marta: curious on multilingual performance — which of those handle low-resource languages better?
[02:14] Priya: in our experience: Mistral variants are good generalists but can drop on Japanese; Falcon family is better on longer context and some non-Latin scripts, Llama 2 13B quantized will be weakest on esoteric languages unless fine-tuned. we should consider adding an instruction-tuned or finetuned variant for Spanish/Portuguese if initial runs lag.
[02:34] Liam: cost — what's rough per-1M-token cost for hosted vs dedicated?
[02:38] Jordan: rough back-of-envelope: hosted Mistral-ish with batching ~ $120-$180 per 1M tokens; Falcon-40B hosted closer to $400-$600 per 1M tokens unless quantized/dedicated; Llama2-13B quantized on dedicated could be sub-$100 per 1M depending on utilization. we'll provide more exact numbers in the sheet.
[02:58] Sasha: tradeoff question — if we pick Llama2-13B quantized cheap but quality risk, can Redwood provide fallback routing to a higher-quality hosted model for critical customers?
[03:07] Priya: yes, smart routing we can do: route by customer tier or route by confidence threshold and auto-fallback to a stronger variant. that's part of the POC config we can demo.
[03:16] Marta: benchmarks — what dataset do you want? we can share 500 prompt pairs plus 100 longer chats for edge cases.
[03:22] Priya: perfect. we'll use your real prompts (anonymized) plus a synthetic multilingual slice. runner will measure latency p50/p95, token cost, ROUGE and an automated semantic-sim metric, plus human eval on top-100.
[03:34] Ethan: timeline — can we kick off next week? our internal SRE may need to approve inbound runners to our VPC if dedicated.
[03:41] Jordan: timeline proposed: Jordan shares shortlist + pricing by Fri 2026-04-09; Priya shares bench plan and script by Mon 2026-04-12; customer provides prompts by Sat 2026-04-10; kickoff bench week of 2026-04-13; 2-week run finishing 2026-04-27; decision week of 2026-05-04.
[03:58] Marta: sounds good. question on privacy: will Redwood store prompts?
[04:02] Jordan: hosted will not store prompts beyond ephemeral caching for performance; for Dedicated/Private we can disable logs and integrate KMS. we'll send SOC2 + security whitepaper.
[04:12] Liam: any concerns around KV cache size with 1.2k token contexts?
[04:16] Priya: KV cache scales with context, but our runtime handles continuous batching and eviction; for the POC we'll use baseline config and tune if p95 rises. we'll also test sequence-length distribution to pick kernels.
[04:28] Marta: is there an option to run a smaller fine-tune on top of an open model for Spanish?
[04:33] Priya: yes, we can do lightweight LoRA-style tuning on a small subset, but that adds time and complexity — for POC we recommend evaluating base models first, then do a quick 1-2 epoch LoRA if needed.
[04:45] Jordan: ok, any other blockers?
[04:47] Sasha: procurement wants vendor questionnaire — we'll send it after the call.
[04:50] Ethan: also please include an option for private deployment if the cost and compliance require.
[04:54] Jordan: will do.
[04:56] Marta: recap — POC success criteria: p50 < 350ms, quality >= baseline ROUGE, cost target TBD, pass EU residency + log/audit checks. run 2-week bench on 3 models: Mistral-ish 7B, Falcon-40B instruct variant, Llama2-13B quantized. Redwood to provide scripts, pricing and routing options.
[05:10] Jordan: great — we'll follow up with the deck, model shortlist and benchmark plan. thanks everyone.

End of call.
